title: Pizza with extra meat, thin crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with extra meat on a thin crust is a classic Italian pizza made with a crisp, thin dough, topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and a generous assortment of meats: ham, sausage, bacon, and ground beef. Perfect for meat lovers seeking a hearty bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin crust bakes quickly and stays crunchy.
Extra meat is often a mix of several sausage types to enhance flavor complexity.
Traditional ovens bake pizza at 250‑300 °C, giving the crust a golden hue.
In Italy similar versions are called “pizza alla carne” and are served as a “speciale”.
Thin crust contains fewer calories than a thick crust, but the added meat keeps the overall calorie count high.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat toppings provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat and bacon are good sources of heme iron, helping prevent anemia.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella supplies calcium, important for bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat ingredients are rich in B6 and B12 vitamins, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene from tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Meat and cheese can raise saturated fat intake, which may be undesirable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Sausages and bacon are often salty, potentially contributing to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A serving can exceed 800 kcal due to the abundance of meat and cheese.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Thin crust is typically made from wheat flour, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, cut into slices. For added freshness, top with raw vegetables such as arugula or cherry tomatoes after baking. Optional finishes include grated Parmesan or a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore the crust’s crispness.
